content: Bounded agentic optimization loops share architecture with AutoML HPO: (1) step/trial budget as the primary hard stop (max_steps, max_trials, time_budget_s); (2) no-improvement window as the soft stop (patience N steps without target diagnostic improving by threshold delta); (3) plateau detection when metric variance over last K steps < epsilon; (4) oscillation guard: track per-step delta; if consecutive deltas alternate sign, declare oscillation and halt or shrink step size. In pure HPO (Optuna/Ray Tune), Bayesian optimization and ASHA/HyperBand add surrogate-model-guided search not applicable when the coordinator is LLM-based. Key difference for LLM-free-compute coordinator: no surrogate model, no Bayesian posterior, no parallel trials; the loop is sequential propose→apply→measure. Stopping signals that DO apply: max_steps hard budget, patience-based no-improvement halt, explicit target_diagnostic threshold (stop when diag >= goal), oscillation guard (alternate-sign delta). Stopping signals that DON'T apply: multi-fidelity resource allocation (ASHA), surrogate model expected improvement, parallel trial pruning (HyperBand). Multi-objective target: compare on one primary diagnostic; optionally report secondary diagnostics — do not aggregate into a single scalar without user direction. Human-in-the-loop checkpoints: configurable via callback/return_on_each_step param or after N steps.
